instrument: GRADE for diagnostic test accuracy (Schunemann et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2020;122:129-141 and 142-152)

risk_of_bias.reason: 18 of 18 studies are at high risk of bias in at least one QUADAS-2 domain (100%)

indirectness.reason: 18 of 18 studies raise high applicability concern for patient selection (100%): the pooled contrast is case versus healthy control, not the differential diagnosis a clinician faces

imprecision.reason: 95% modified Hartung-Knapp (mHK) interval around the primary pooled AUC (18 studies) spans 0.080 (0.772-0.852); 95% prediction interval 0.620-0.923

publication_bias.reason: Egger p = 0.0304 (one estimate per study) and 0.0038 (every estimate); small-study effects on both pools (not itself proof of publication bias)

risk_of_bias.reason: 19 of 19 studies are at high risk of bias in at least one QUADAS-2 domain (100%)

indirectness.reason: 19 of 19 studies raise high applicability concern for patient selection (100%): the pooled contrast is case versus healthy control, not the differential diagnosis a clinician faces

imprecision.reason: 95% modified Hartung-Knapp (mHK) interval around the primary pooled AUC (19 studies) spans 0.107 (0.741-0.848); 95% prediction interval 0.524-0.936

bivariate_summary_of_findings_scope: exploratory, AD and PD combined, 19 independent studies with a paired sensitivity and specificity; not disease-specific and not the basis for either disease's GRADE rating above
reading_en: AD and PD are rated separately because they are different diagnostic questions with different evidence bases (18 AD and 19 PD studies in the primary, circulating AUC pool), and a single combined verdict would obscure that PD's evidence is more heterogeneous (I2 81.1% versus AD's 78.5%). Both ratings are very low, driven by the same structural facts: every study is a case-versus-healthy-control design, no study pre-specified its positivity threshold, and heterogeneity is high to extreme. The combined bivariate summary of findings below is a secondary, exploratory illustration of what a pooled operating point would imply clinically, drawn from only 19 studies, and should not be read as a validated clinical accuracy for either disease individually.
reading_pt: AD e PD sao classificadas separadamente porque sao perguntas diagnosticas diferentes com bases de evidencia diferentes (18 estudos de AD e 19 de PD no pool primario circulante de AUC), e um veredito unico combinado esconderia que a evidencia de PD e mais heterogenea (I2 81.1% contra 78.5% de AD). As duas classificacoes sao muito baixas, guiadas pelos mesmos fatos estruturais: todo estudo e um desenho caso-versus-controle-saudavel, o limiar de positividade nao foi pre-especificado por nenhum estudo, e a heterogeneidade e alta a extrema. A tabela de resumo de achados bivariada combinada abaixo e uma ilustracao secundaria e exploratoria do que um ponto de operacao agrupado implicaria clinicamente, tirada de apenas 19 estudos, e nao deve ser lida como uma acuracia clinica validada para nenhuma das duas doencas isoladamente.
